//: Type-checks the autonomous-ops scripts.
WHY THIS EXISTS: nothing type-checked scripts/ at all. CI's `lint` job covers
middleware/src + realtime/src, and the only `typecheck` job covers `display`.
`pnpm test:ops` runs under tsx, which STRIPS types without checking them. So a
type error in production ops code reached main silently — one already did:
lib/state.ts used `Incident` without importing it.
Scope is all of scripts/ EXCEPT *.spec.ts. The spec files are jest-based and
would need jest globals in `types`; everything else — including the live PM2
cron agents in scripts/agents — type-checks clean, so the gate costs nothing.
A first draft scoped this to scripts/ops only, justified by scripts/agents
supposedly carrying implicit-any errors and unresolved @vizora/database. Review
showed that was an environment artifact of an UNBUILT packages/database/dist,
not a property of the code: with dist built, scripts/agents has zero of either.
Recording it because the same artifact will mislead the next person who runs
tsc here without building first.
Two exclusions, each for a stated reason rather than convenience:
release/**        owned by the vizora-tv release workstream; its test imports a
.mjs with no declaration file. Not this change's surface.
seed-production.ts BROKEN against the current schema — it writes Plan.monthlyPrice
and Plan.yearlyPrice, which do not exist; the model has
priceUsdMonthly / priceUsdYearly / priceInrMonthly /
priceInrYearly. It would throw at runtime. Excluded rather than
silently fixed because choosing the missing INR/USD values is a
data decision, not a mechanical one. It is referenced from no
package.json script, ecosystem entry, workflow or doc.
Settings mirror what the ops code is actually executed with: ESM, bundler
resolution (so `./x.js` specifiers resolve to `./x.ts`, as tsx does).
